CORRECTED same-day, 2026-08-18 (live-failure fix): this key was first synthesized as a bare 'refunds: []' list, shaped to match the catalog's selectionPath at the time ("returns.nodes.refunds.id", no '.nodes'). That selectionPath was itself wrong — Return.refunds is a RefundConnection, not a plain list — and a real reconciliation run against a live store proved it: Shopify's GraphQL validator rejected the query outright with "Field 'id' doesn't exist on type 'RefundConnection'". Because this fixture's 'refunds: []' happened to be shaped like the (wrong) query's expected result, every fixture-based test kept passing throughout — the fixture validated the code against its own mistaken assumption instead of against Shopify's actual schema. Reshaped below to 'refunds: {"nodes": []}', the real connection form the corrected selectionPath ("returns.nodes.refunds.nodes.id") now selects. Catching this class of error needs a rendered-query-document assertion, not a fixture — see ShopifySourceCatalogAndQueryBuilderTests.returnRefsQuerySelectsTheNestedRefundsConnectionAsNodesNotAsAPlainId.
